## 固定收益開篇論點

7月29日美國公債收盤終結先前連續三個交易日的漲勢，政策定價與存續期間走勢呈現異常鮮明的分化。Fed將目標區間維持在3.5%至3.75%後，2年期殖利率下跌4個基點至4.22%；5年期卻上升2個基點至4.37%，10年期攀升6個基點至4.67%，30年期更跳升11個基點至5.20%。2s10s因而陡峭化10個基點至45個基點，2s30s陡峭化15個基點至98個基點，一舉逆轉此前油價降溫帶動、同時壓低政策利率與存續期間風險補償的債市漲勢。

市場的核心矛盾不只是Fed按兵不動、三位官員主張升息。9比3的決議排除立即升息的尾部風險，帶動前端殖利率下行，但主席Kevin Warsh幾乎未說明緊縮立場何時會化為行動，反而認為市場殖利率上升已是正在發揮作用的緊縮機制之一。投資人因此將可能升息的時點往後推，同時在長端要求更高的通膨與政策可信度補償。交換市場顯示9月升息機率約為60%，相較決議前立即升息機率約40%；直到12月才完全反映一次升息。

通膨定價清楚呈現市場的質疑。10年期實質殖利率持平於2.41%，因此10年期名目殖利率上升的6個基點全數來自損益兩平通膨率走高至2.26%。更長天期方面，30年期實質殖利率上升6個基點至2.98%，5年期實質殖利率則下跌6個基點至2.13%。殖利率曲線因而將近期政策壓力緩解，與更沉重的通膨及實質存續期間負擔區隔開來。美國與伊朗敵對行動再起後，Brent反彈7.37%至$90.29，WTI上漲6.35%至$84.29，進一步加深長端對延後行動的質疑。

信用市場帶來另一條明確的供給傳導管道，而非單純跟隨美國公債賣壓。長存續期間資產承受更大的利率衝擊，LQD下跌0.57%，跌幅高於HYG與JNK約0.23%的跌幅。紐約聯準銀行週三發布的一項指標顯示，在7月高評級債券發行額創下$1,320億紀錄之際，投資級市場失序程度升至2023年11月以來最高。CoreWeave一筆$26億AI貸款擴大定價利差並強化契約文件；軟體業借款人則在攤還與擔保品保障上讓步。融資管道仍然暢通，但凡是AI支出或科技顛覆提高不確定性的領域，議價權都已轉向貸款人。

全球證據顯示，美國走勢不能解讀為普遍性的通膨重新定價。澳洲核心通膨低於預期，市場隱含的2026年RBA再度升息機率由逾90%降至約50%，3年期殖利率下跌11個基點。歐元區薪資預測仍遠低於2024年高點，即使ECB仍保留9月緊縮的可能性。日本則朝相反方向發展：薪資漲幅擴及更多勞工，支持BOJ進一步正常化，日本最大退休基金也正調整操作，以因應更高的JGB波動。美國長端賣壓雖然劇烈，海外殖利率曲線仍有顯著分歧。

因此，收盤所建立的市場狀態比前一日油價帶動的緩解行情更脆弱。Fed事件的即時風險下降，但市場對通膨補償、長端實質殖利率、財政供給預期與AI相關信用承接都提出更高要求。美元走弱、新興市場貨幣走強，顯示這並非全面性的美元流動性緊縮；壓力反而轉向長天期折現率，以及政策路徑訊號不清、卻仍要求市場承擔通膨風險的政策機構可信度。

## 美國公債利率、Fed定價、實質殖利率與曲線結構

前端正確反映實際按兵不動與會前機率分布之間的差異。FOMC連續第七個月將聯邦基金利率區間維持在3.5%至3.75%；達拉斯聯準銀行總裁Lorie Logan、克里夫蘭聯準銀行總裁Beth Hammack與明尼亞波利斯聯準銀行總裁Neel Kashkari投下異議票，主張升息25個基點。2年期殖利率下跌4個基點至4.22%，多個代表性國庫券天期的殖利率亦下跌5至9個基點，消除了立即升息所附帶的溢價。三票異議則使這波緩解未被解讀為寬鬆訊號。

長端將同一項決議解讀為延後緊縮。Warsh重申2%的目標，否定採用較寬鬆目標的構想，卻未承諾升息。他認為金融條件收緊已發揮作用，等於把更多調整責任交給市場殖利率。30年期殖利率盤中一度逼近5.23%，收於5.20%，落在2007年以來最高的收盤區域。20年期以上美國公債指數下跌1.64%，1至3年期指數則上漲0.06%，證實存續期間分化的幅度，且不影響現券殖利率所傳達的訊號。

曲線變化之大，本身即帶有明確的政策意涵。2s10s斜率由35個基點擴大至45個基點，2s30s則由83個基點擴大至98個基點。即使前端債券上漲，5年期殖利率仍上升，顯示轉折點位於即時政策定價與承載未來數年通膨及供給風險的天期之間。2s10s30s蝶式利差移動5個基點至-8個基點，與10年期受到長端重新定價牽引一致。不過，主要訊號仍是會後出現的歷史性陡峭化，而非局部相對價值錯位。

抗通膨美國公債呈現兩種不同期限的走勢。10年期名目殖利率上升6個基點，實質殖利率維持2.41%，使損益兩平通膨率上升6個基點至2.26%。這逆轉前一日收盤走勢；當時油價壓力緩解，同時壓低名目殖利率與實質折現率。30年期實質殖利率上升6個基點至2.98%，20年期上升4個基點至2.76%；相較之下，5年期與7年期實質殖利率分別下跌6個與4個基點。即時政策壓力緩解，卻與更高的長期實質門檻同時存在。

油價是當日最直接的通膨催化因素。美國與伊朗交戰的暫歇告終，華府揚言強力回應美軍遭受的攻擊，WTI因而升至$84.29，Brent升至$90.29。兩項合約仍低於前一週高點，但過去1個月分別上漲21.75%與25.42%。單日再度上漲逾6%，削弱先前三天原油崩跌已持久降低能源衝擊的假設，也提高僅靠金融條件因應通膨的成本。

政策機率分布僅靠將升息時點往後移而收斂。會議前，儘管幾乎所有受訪經濟學家都預期按兵不動，市場仍賦予立即升息約35%至40%的機率。會後，交換市場顯示9月升息機率接近60%，直到12月才完全反映一次升息。升息時點不像前一日收盤時那樣前置；當時市場已完全反映9月升息，但緊縮路徑依然存在。三票異議與高於目標的通膨維持政策方向；Warsh提供的指引有限且倚賴市場自行緊縮，使確切日期更不確定。

交易活動符合實質重新定價，而非交投清淡造成的收盤波動，但無法據此判斷投資人方向。FINRA通報名目附息債券成交面額達$1.15兆，較7月28日增加10.3%。20年期以上天期的交易活動增加36.9%，7至10年期區間增加30.4%，3至5年期成交面額則減少14.2%。交易集中在長端與基準中期區間，與殖利率調整最大之處吻合，但仍無法判定最終投資人是增加或減少部位。

財政供給仍是長端溢價尚未解決的驅動因素。JPMorgan估計，未來四個會計年度的資金缺口為$3.7兆，並認為美國財政部最終必須放寬票息債標售規模將「至少在未來數季」維持穩定的指引。策略師預期官員不會在下次季度再融資時修改這項說法，因為期中選舉前暗示長天期供給增加，本身就可能使殖利率曲線陡峭化。維持原有措辭可延後公告效應，卻無法消除根本融資需求。

因此，利率市場的結論比2年期殖利率下降所呈現的更為緊縮。Fed消除近期尾部風險，卻未確認政策轉向寬鬆；市場將尚未解決的通膨問題轉移至損益兩平通膨率、長端實質殖利率與大幅陡峭化的曲線。2年、5年、10年與30年期殖利率過去1個月分別變動15、25、29與33個基點，顯示重新定價已延伸甚廣。週三按兵不動釐清當前利率，卻使等待所需付出的未來代價更不確定。

## 信用、融資與初級市場承接

整體信用市場走弱，走勢以存續期間為主；投資級市場運作出現可量化的惡化，又使情況更加複雜。LQD下跌0.57%，HYG與JNK則均下跌0.23%。20年期以上AAA至A級公司債指數下跌1.34%，同類BBB級指數下跌1.30%，同期長天期美國公債指數下跌1.64%。這些指數報酬顯示長端殖利率上升帶來的按市價評價負擔。直接利差資料則帶來額外的信用訊號：投資級利差為80個基點，高於7月初的74個基點。

紐約聯準銀行的公司債市場困境指數，區分整體穩定與高評級債券承壓。截至7月24日，整體指標由6月底的0.16降至0.15，投資級子指數則由0.25升至0.30，達到2023年11月以來最高點。高評級讀數約位於歷史第68百分位。7月發行額創下約$1,320億紀錄，部分由籌措AI投資資金的科技業借款人帶動，使新券定價與次級市場流動性惡化，但未造成全市場失序。

CoreWeave顯示，投資人對AI擔保品的熱情能多快轉化為對更高現金殖利率與更嚴密契約文件的要求。其$26億延遲動用定期貸款的定價利差最多擴大125個基點，最高達基準利率加碼550個基點。發行價格由99降至97，且在週四訂單截止前強化債權人保障。這筆貸款用於GPU及其他設備，支應Anthropic、Jane Street與Hudson River Trading以照付不議合約承租的運算容量；利息僅按實際動用資金計收。

這筆融資的經濟邏輯仍與積極擴張計畫緊密相連。CoreWeave預計今年投入逾$340億於AI基礎設施，其5年期違約保障成本7月上升逾50%，來到去年12月以來最高。此前一筆$31億GPU擔保融資吸引$190億訂單，因此最新讓利反映承接情況出現重大變化，而非該平台向來無法取得融資。投資人正在區分實體設備、合約收入，以及提前於需求擴建所需的槓桿。

這股變化也延伸至面臨AI競爭威脅的軟體業者。貸款人要求防範擔保品移轉與選擇性債務回購後，Proofpoint重整一筆$50億修約展期交易。公司同意納入「全方位阻擋條款」（omni blocker）、未來回購要約同等對待，以及修改約兩打貸款條款。擬議展期將2028年到期日延至2030年，定價為基準利率加碼425至450個基點，發行價格98至98.5。

Proofpoint的條件反映更廣泛的到期與議價問題。約$3,000億美國槓桿貸款將於2028年到期，其中近三分之一與科技公司相關，許多是由私募股權支持、在2021年取得融資的軟體業借款人。Imprivata近期將一筆$12億貸款展期，支付基準利率加碼375個基點，高於原先的300個基點。眼前疑慮不只在於AI是否會壓低未來營收，更在於借款人能否在不移轉擔保品、不偏袒特定貸款人，也不將價值移出現有資本結構的情況下再融資。

歐洲槓桿融資也透過預定償還本金，呈現相同的貸款人偏好。Paysafe提出每年攤還原始本金的5%，以將$8.14億與5.86億歐元定期貸款展延兩年至2030年。該交易支付基準利率加碼500個基點，並允許貸款人按95的價格承作、到期償還時可能收回100。投資人也表示，如果think-cell展延其7.2億歐元貸款，他們將要求加入攤還；該貸款目前支付Euribor加碼425個基點。

具實質意義的攤還條款自2008年以來在歐洲罕見，如今回歸，使風險由單一到期再融資轉向較早收回現金，也區分出有獲利、能償債的軟體業借款人，與仰賴不斷展期的結構。CLO需求仍可削弱貸款人的議價能力：約30%投資人拒絕Carlyle支持的AutoForm展期，但更廣泛的需求使其6.72億歐元定期貸款利差收窄，並將到期日延至2032年。換取保障的代價正在上升，但貸款供給稀少，仍使緊縮程度無法全面一致。

SoftBank的日圓發債顯示，融資多元化仍可實現，只是代價清楚可見。公司發行900億日圓債券，將3年期券規模提高至800億日圓，5年期維持100億日圓。票面利率分別為3.270%與3.886%，較JGB加碼165與190個基點，是今年國內企業發行人在相同天期支付的最高水準。升息環境下，投資人偏好較短天期，5年期最終需求僅約為發行額的1.2倍。

此次發債有助SoftBank為逾$600億的OpenAI承諾提供資金，另有一筆已有21家貸款機構加入的$400億過渡性貸款。此前至少$60億保證金融資的洽談也陷入停滯，早先$100億的目標已遭下修。橫跨日圓、美元、歐元、零售次順位債與銀行市場取得資金，可降低對單一管道的依賴；但高票息與偏好短天期顯示，融資來源廣泛仍未消除市場對槓桿、存續期間及AI承諾過度集中的疑慮。

銀行也在把風險移出資產負債表，以保留放款容量。ING準備對約$100億貸款進行significant risk transfer，其中約$60億為涵蓋資料中心的美國與歐洲專案融資，另有€35億Netherlands中小企業曝險。風險部位分別約占參考資產組合7%與6%；全球SRT發行量預估由2025年$410億升至2026年創紀錄的$450億。超過10%的票息吸引投資人，但這項機制只是轉移第一損失曝險，並未消除底層信用循環。Private credit流入保險資產負債表的管道，也面臨治理限制。Delaware Life重列報告後，評級機構估計關係人資產已占總資產40%至42%，而不是原先約3%至5%。監管機構若更廣泛檢視關係人持有部位，即使借款人違約率未變，也可能減緩資產管理公司把私人貸款配置到保險公司的速度。信用市場流動性仍正常運作，但投資人已不再照單全收。高評級供給使市場運作承壓，CoreWeave付出更高成本並強化契約文件，軟體業貸款人重新取得擔保品與還款保障，SoftBank則以今年相同天期國內最高票息拓展融資來源。共同機制並非違約迫在眉睫，而是當大型資本計畫、再融資高峰與科技不確定性競逐相同的資產負債表時，市場所要求的補償更高、第一損失曝險被轉移，控制權也更嚴。

## 全球存續期間、央行與財政傳導

澳洲是反駁美國通膨式陡峭化最清楚的案例。第二季截尾平均CPI年增3.6%，低於3.7%的市場共識；季增0.8%，也低於0.9%的預測。交易員將今年RBA再度升息的機率由逾90%降至約50%，澳幣最多下跌0.5%，政策敏感的3年期殖利率下跌11個基點。數據使RBA在2026年稍早三度升息後，於8月11日會議重新取得觀望空間。

通膨組成顯示，這份緩解仍有條件。受進口能源壓力降低與臨時燃油稅減免協助，可貿易財通膨年增率僅1.5%，不可貿易項目通膨則達4.9%。核心通膨也仍高於RBA的2%至3%目標區間，而油價再度上漲，挑戰外部通膨成分將持續下降的假設。澳洲殖利率曲線反映的是較溫和的國內數據，並非緊縮風險告終。

歐元區薪資數據降低出現2022年式二輪效應的機率，但未排除9月政策行動。ECB追蹤指標預測，協議薪資增幅在第三季與第四季為2.6%，2027年第一季為2.7%，遠低於2024年的5.2%高點。官員表示，增幅部分來自比較基期的機械性變化，因舊有一次性給付正退出比較。薪資壓力穩定，讓ECB有時間區分暫時性能源通膨與持續性通膨；不過，如果前景未改善，決策官員仍準備再次升息。

英國的高借款成本與民間信用需求韌性並存，處境較不舒適。6月房貸核准件數由逾兩年低點回升至58,200件，高於57,100件的市場共識；無擔保借款增加18億英鎊。然而，5年期房貸平均利率在7月29日升至5.66%，高於伊朗戰爭前的4.83%。家庭與企業借款尚未崩跌，BOE因此必須在成長疲弱與能源成本轉嫁之間權衡，無法從需求面獲得明確的寬鬆理由。

日本的薪資與機構買方證據都支持國內存續期間市場進入波動更高的狀態。勞動主管機關小組建議，將全國最低工資提高4.9%至每小時1,176日圓，增加55日圓，調幅為史上第二高。漲幅低於去年的6.3%，但在主要工會連續第三年爭取到逾5%加薪後，可將薪資成長擴及大型雇主以外的勞工。BOJ評估6月將政策利率升至1%的影響之際，這進一步強化其薪資—物價論點。

GPIF的因應方式顯示買方結構如何調整。該基金在截至3月的一年內，日本債券部位虧損5.1%，但整體報酬仍達16.5%；其後五年來首度委任三家主動式國內債券經理人。國內債券25%的配置目標，使其具備支撐市場的規模，但主動委任可更靈活調整天期與信用曝險。日本殖利率走高可吸引國內儲蓄，卻會減少日本機構過去自動配置於美國公債等海外長存續期間資產的需求。

Canada在利率維持不變的決策內部，也呈現政策分歧。Bank of Canada連續第6次會議把利率維持在2.25%，並預估經濟成長率將由2026年0.7%，加速至2027年與2028年均為1.8%。部分官員質疑復甦是否持久，另一些則擔心中期通膨預期上移；但經濟供給過剩、單位勞動成本成長放緩與租金通膨下降，提供相反證據。現行政策仍被認為適當，但會議紀要顯示，下一步取決於復甦與通膨張力的哪一側持續。全球整體脈動，是各市場圍繞共同能源衝擊呈現分歧。澳洲出現由數據確實帶動的漲勢，歐元區薪資不支持通膨必然加速，英國信用需求則削弱快速寬鬆的理由。日本薪資成長範圍擴大、機構調整操作，支持政策持續正常化。這些傳導管道不會直接推高美國殖利率，但海外政策利率與本國債券報酬仍具足夠競爭力，使美國公債長端無法仰賴全球一致的存續期間買盤。

## 新興市場主權債、美元流動性與債務管理風險

新興市場呈現貨幣壓力緩解、硬通貨長存續期間債券下跌的分化。Fed按兵不動後，一項新興市場貨幣指數上漲0.3%，美元指數則下跌0.59%至100.78。EMB仍下跌0.66%，15年期以上新興市場美元主權債指數也因長天期美國公債殖利率上升壓過美元走弱而下跌0.60%。共同衝擊因此來自長端折現率，而非美元流動性普遍短缺。

玻利維亞顯示，即使獲得政策支持，只要市場仍質疑執行，效力就有其極限。IMF宣布就一項新的$19億計畫達成協議後，該國債券小幅走低。市場反應不像區域性融資管道關閉；新興市場貨幣走強，美元也走弱。這反而顯示，當投資人尚未看到資產負債表路徑確實改善時，僅有官方融資的公告並不能消除特定主權國家的執行與債務可持續性疑慮。

巴西面臨通膨降溫與需求有韌性之間的另一種矛盾。7月上旬消費者通膨由6月中旬的4.8%降至4.52%，強化市場對8月5日連續第四次降息25個基點至14%的預期。就業市場穩健，加上政府財政與信用刺激，仍可能使需求相對3%目標保持強勁。美國前端殖利率下降提供部分空間，但美元長端殖利率走高、油價反彈，使巴西降息路徑仍取決於國內通膨下降，而非僅靠全球環境緩解。

印度銀行資本顯示本幣市場具備選擇性承接能力。印度國家銀行在離開市場近兩年後，透過永續型額外第一類資本債券籌得469.1億印度盧比。該債券票面利率7.75%、5年後可贖回，在當地評為AA+，投標金額超過300億印度盧比基礎規模的兩倍。這些資本支應其成長近17%、超過49兆印度盧比的放款組合。這是銀行風險而非主權風險，卻顯示即使美元長存續期間資產走弱，國內儲蓄仍能支應資產負債表擴張。

Philippines顯示，減稅可能在債券市場准入真正關閉前，就削弱既定財政整頓路徑。勞工所得稅減免每年可能減少最高600億披索、約$9.78億收入，而政府原已規劃2026年借款2.68兆披索。第1季債務達GDP的65.2%，高於發展中經濟體常用的60%門檻；便宜的疫情期間債務以現行殖利率再融資後，利息支出占收入比重也上升。因此，若要把赤字由2025年GDP的5.6%，降至2030年的3.5%，減稅同時必須搭配替代收入或支出控制。India則採取相反方向，準備立法正式確認外國投資人購買主權債的稅務減免，以財政政策擴大外部買方，而非提供家庭減稅。措施可能改善投資人參與，但最終融資效果仍須由法案通過與實際資金流證明，不能只看立法計畫。因此，新興市場環境既非全面風險偏好升溫，也不是共同的融資斷裂。貨幣市場歡迎Fed按兵不動，但硬通貨債券仍暴露於30年期美國公債衝擊。玻利維亞、巴西與印度國家銀行進一步區分官方計畫可信度、國內政策空間與本地資本承接。美元下跌減輕一項外部限制，卻未消除長存續期間重新定價或各國特有的資產負債表考驗。

## 跨資產

跨資產走勢強化通膨與存續期間的解讀，而非單純的成長恐慌。地緣政治緊張再起，Brent上漲7.37%，WTI上漲6.35%，大幅削弱此前美國公債漲勢賴以成立的油價降溫前提。黃金上漲2.78%至$4,148.60，美元下跌0.59%。油價與金價走高、美元走弱，同時長端殖利率上升，符合通膨與政策可信度溢價擴大，而非市場普遍追逐美元現金。

股票市場提供另一項獨立的緊縮信號。S&P 500下跌1.52%，Nasdaq 100下跌2.06%，半導體指數下跌5.33%，連續第五個交易日走低。VIX上漲13.45%至20.66。半導體類股過去1週下跌15.82%，過去1個月下跌20.87%，將市場對AI資本報酬的疑慮，與信用市場要求更大折價、更強契約保障及提早償還本金連結起來。Fed決議後大盤下跌，顯示前端殖利率下降並未轉化為金融條件寬鬆。

信用債與新興市場基金下跌，卻未呈現無差別清算的特徵。高收益債ETF跌幅遠小於長存續期間較高的LQD，新興市場貨幣上漲，美元則走弱。因此，跨資產檢驗支持兩個集中的壓力點：一是能源與政策可信度對長天期主權債殖利率的壓力，二是AI支出與科技顛覆對科技相關風險的壓力；並不支持整體經濟融資管道全面崩潰。

## 前瞻市場意涵

7月31日公布的就業成本指數，以及其後通膨與勞動市場數據，將決定政策時點造成的殖利率曲線分化能否延續。如果薪資或物價數據持續強勁，且Brent維持在$90附近或以上，9月升息仍會是選項，並迫使2年期殖利率逆轉會後跌勢；若勞動成本路徑轉弱且油價再度降溫，前端便可延續漲勢。更重要的可信度門檻位於較長天期：10年期損益兩平通膨率與20至30年期實質殖利率必須停止上升，延後升息才會被視為耐心，而非喪失通膨控制。下次季度再融資則為同一項考驗增添供給面。維持票息債規模將「至少在未來數季」不變的說法，或可抑制即時公告衝擊；若措辭使增加長天期供給的時點提前，則會在未來四年估計$3.7兆資金缺口的背景下，進一步強化2s30s陡峭化。

CoreWeave週四訂單截止，以及一筆與Microsoft承租的資料中心相關、可能達$54億的QTS融資，將檢驗AI信用是否找到新的出清水準。CoreWeave需要在最高為基準利率加碼550個基點、發行價格97且保障條款加強的條件下吸引需求，才能證明讓利仍足以抵銷市場對年度基礎設施支出逾$340億的疑慮。QTS預計發行約$49億擔保債券與一筆$5億定期貸款；該公司近期貸款價格已由99.5跌至97.75，4月發行債券相對美國公債的利差則由約138個基點擴大至239個基點。若次級市場價格穩定、新券讓利受控，壓力仍可集中在結構與價格；若再度延後、折價擴大，或市場要求更多債權人控制權，投資級與槓桿貸款的承接問題就會加深。

BOE於7月30日、BOJ於7月31日公布決議，將決定海外存續期間是否成為美國資產負債表更強的競爭者。即使5年期房貸平均利率為5.66%、借款仍具韌性，BOE若按兵不動並對能源成本轉嫁將消退表示有信心，就必須帶動英國公債殖利率下降；否則英國殖利率曲線仍會保留通膨與財政溢價。BOJ在6月將政策利率升至1%後，預計本次按兵不動，但指引必須調和擬議最低工資上調4.9%與日圓疲弱帶來的進口通膨。若政策路徑能穩定日圓且不再引發失序的JGB賣壓，將降低全球期限溢價壓力。日本殖利率上升或日圓再度走弱，則會使本國報酬持續吸引日本機構，讓美國公債長端更難獲得海外需求支撐。

## Opening Fixed-Income Thesis

The July 29 Treasury close broke the prior three-session rally through an unusually sharp policy-versus-duration split. The 2-year yield fell 4 basis points to 4.22% after the Fed held its target range at 3.5% to 3.75%, yet the 5-year rose 2 basis points to 4.37%, the 10-year climbed 6 basis points to 4.67%, and the 30-year jumped 11 basis points to 5.20%. The resulting 10-basis-point steepening in 2s10s to 45 basis points and 15-basis-point steepening in 2s30s to 98 marked a reversal from oil-relief rallies that had lowered both policy and duration compensation.

The central tension was not simply that the Fed held while three officials preferred a hike. The 9-3 decision removed an immediate tightening tail and pulled the front end lower, but Chairman Kevin Warsh offered little guidance on when restraint might become action. He instead treated the rise in market yields as part of the tightening already under way. Investors responded by moving the likely hike later while charging more at the long end for inflation and policy credibility. Swaps left roughly a 60% probability of a September increase, compared with about 40% odds of an immediate move before the decision, and did not fully price a hike until December.

Inflation pricing made the market's challenge explicit. The 10-year real yield was unchanged at 2.41%, so the full 6-basis-point rise in the nominal 10-year came through a higher breakeven, to 2.26%. Farther out, the 30-year real yield rose 6 basis points to 2.98%, while the 5-year real yield fell 6 basis points to 2.13%. The curve therefore separated near-term relief from a larger inflation and real-duration burden. Brent's 7.37% rebound to $90.29 and WTI's 6.35% rise to $84.29, after renewed US-Iran hostilities, reinforced the long-end objection to postponing action.

Credit added a distinct supply channel rather than merely echoing the Treasury selloff. LQD fell 0.57%, more than the roughly 0.23% declines in HYG and JNK, as long-duration assets absorbed the larger rates shock. A New York Fed measure released Wednesday showed investment-grade market dysfunction at its highest since November 2023 amid a record $132 billion of July high-grade issuance. CoreWeave widened pricing and strengthened documentation on a $2.6 billion AI loan, while software borrowers conceded amortization and collateral protections. Financing remained available, but the balance of power moved toward lenders where AI spending or disruption increased uncertainty.

Global evidence prevented the US move from being read as a universal inflation repricing. Australian core inflation undershot expectations and cut the market-implied chance of another 2026 RBA hike to about 50% from more than 90%, pulling the 3-year yield down 11 basis points. Euro-area wage projections remained far below their 2024 peak even as the ECB kept September tightening possible. Japan moved in the opposite direction: broader wage gains supported further BOJ normalization, and its largest pension fund was adapting to greater JGB volatility. The US long-end selloff was severe, but foreign curves retained meaningful dispersion.

The close consequently established a more fragile regime than the prior day's oil-led relief. Immediate Fed-event risk fell, but inflation compensation, long real yields, fiscal supply expectations and AI-related credit absorption all became more demanding. A weaker dollar and firmer emerging-market currencies showed that this was not a generalized dollar-liquidity seizure. The constraint migrated instead toward long-maturity discount rates and the credibility of institutions asking markets to absorb inflation risk without a clearly signaled policy path.

## UST Rates, Fed Pricing, Real Yields, And Curve Structure

The front end correctly registered the difference between a realized hold and the pre-meeting distribution. The FOMC kept the funds range at 3.5% to 3.75% for a seventh consecutive month, with Dallas Fed President Lorie Logan, Cleveland Fed President Beth Hammack and Minneapolis Fed President Neel Kashkari dissenting for a 25-basis-point increase. The 2-year yield's 4-basis-point fall to 4.22% and declines of 5 to 9 basis points across representative bill maturities removed the premium attached to an immediate hike. The dissents stopped that relief from becoming an easing signal.

The long end interpreted the same decision as deferred restraint. Warsh reiterated the 2% objective and rejected the idea of a softer target, yet he stopped short of committing to a rate increase. His argument that tighter financial conditions had already done useful work placed more of the adjustment onto market yields. The 30-year briefly approached 5.23% and closed at 5.20%, its highest closing region since 2007. The 20-year-plus Treasury index fell 1.64%, compared with a 0.06% gain in the 1-to-3-year index, confirming the scale of the duration divergence without changing the cash-yield interpretation.

Curve changes were large enough to carry policy meaning on their own. The 2s10s slope widened from 35 to 45 basis points, and 2s30s from 83 to 98. The 5-year yield rose despite the front-end rally, locating the turn between immediate policy pricing and the maturities carrying the next several years of inflation and supply risk. The 2s10s30s butterfly moved 5 basis points to -8, consistent with the 10-year being pulled toward the long-end repricing. The main signal, however, was the historic post-meeting steepening rather than a local relative-value dislocation.

Inflation-linked Treasuries showed two different horizons. At 10 years, the nominal yield rose 6 basis points while the real yield stayed at 2.41%, lifting the breakeven by 6 basis points to 2.26%. That reversed the prior close, when oil relief had lowered both the nominal yield and real discount rate. At 30 years, the real yield increased 6 basis points to 2.98%; at 20 years it rose 4 basis points to 2.76%. By contrast, 5- and 7-year real yields fell 6 and 4 basis points. Immediate policy relief coexisted with a higher long-run real hurdle.

Oil supplied the most direct same-session inflation catalyst. WTI rose to $84.29 and Brent to $90.29 after the pause in US-Iran fighting ended and Washington threatened a forceful response to an attack on US military forces. The contracts remained below the prior week's peaks but were still 21.75% and 25.42% higher over 1 month. A renewed daily increase of more than 6% undermined the premise that the previous three-day collapse in crude had durably reduced the energy shock. It also raised the cost of leaving the inflation response to financial conditions.

The policy distribution narrowed only by shifting forward. Before the meeting, markets assigned roughly 35% to 40% odds to an immediate increase despite nearly all surveyed economists expecting a hold. Afterward, swaps placed the September probability near 60%, and a full increase was not embedded until December. That is less front-loaded than the prior close, when a September move was fully priced, but it remains a tightening path. Three dissents and above-target inflation preserved the direction; Warsh's limited guidance and reliance on market tightening made the date less secure.

Trading activity was consistent with a genuine repricing rather than a thin close, though it does not identify investor direction. FINRA reported $1.15 trillion of nominal-coupon par traded, 10.3% more than on July 28. Activity in maturities longer than 20 years rose 36.9%, and the 7-to-10-year bucket increased 30.4%, while 3-to-5-year par declined 14.2%. The concentration in the long and benchmark intermediate sectors matches where the yield adjustment was largest, without resolving whether end investors added exposure or reduced it.

Fiscal supply remained an unresolved contributor to the long-end premium. JPMorgan estimated a $3.7 trillion funding gap over the next four fiscal years and argued that Treasury eventually needs to relax guidance that coupon auction sizes will remain steady for "at least the next several quarters." The strategists expected officials to avoid changing that phrase at the next quarterly refunding because signaling larger duration supply before the midterms could itself steepen the curve. Holding the language steady can defer the announcement effect, but not the underlying financing need.

The rates conclusion is therefore more restrictive than the lower 2-year yield suggests. The Fed removed a near-term tail without validating easier policy, and the market transferred the unresolved inflation problem into breakevens, long real yields and a much steeper curve. One-month changes of 15, 25, 29 and 33 basis points in the 2-, 5-, 10- and 30-year yields show how far the repricing already extends. Wednesday's hold clarified the current rate; it made the future cost of waiting less certain.

## Credit, Funding, And Primary-Market Absorption

Broad credit weakened in a pattern dominated by duration but complicated by a measurable deterioration in investment-grade functioning. LQD fell 0.57%, versus 0.23% declines in both HYG and JNK. The 20-year-plus AAA-to-A corporate index lost 1.34%, and the comparable BBB index fell 1.30%, against a 1.64% decline in the long Treasury index. Those index returns show the mark-to-market burden of higher long yields. Direct spread data supplied the additional credit signal: investment-grade spreads were 80 basis points, up from 74 at the start of July.

The New York Fed's Corporate Bond Market Distress Index separated broad stability from high-grade strain. Through July 24, the overall gauge eased to 0.15 from 0.16 in late June, while the investment-grade sub-index rose to 0.30 from 0.25 and reached its highest point since November 2023. The high-grade reading stood around its 68th historical percentile. Record July issuance of about $132 billion, driven partly by technology borrowers funding AI investment, worsened new-issue pricing and secondary liquidity without producing a market-wide breakdown.

CoreWeave showed how quickly investor enthusiasm for AI collateral can become a demand for cash yield and stronger documents. Pricing on its $2.6 billion delayed-draw term loan widened by as much as 125 basis points to as high as 550 basis points over the benchmark. The offer price fell to 97 cents from 99, and creditor protections were strengthened before Thursday's order deadline. The loan finances GPUs and other equipment for take-or-pay capacity used by Anthropic, Jane Street and Hudson River Trading, with interest charged only as funds are drawn.

The economics remain tied to an aggressive expansion plan. CoreWeave is expected to spend more than $34 billion on AI infrastructure this year, and its 5-year default-protection cost has risen more than 50% in July to the highest since December. An earlier $3.1 billion GPU-backed financing drew $19 billion of orders, so the latest concession is a material change in absorption rather than evidence that the platform never had access. Investors are distinguishing between hard equipment, contracted revenue and the leverage required to build ahead of demand.

That change extends beyond AI infrastructure into software businesses threatened by AI competition. Proofpoint reworked a $5 billion amend-and-extend transaction after lenders pressed for protection against collateral transfers and selective debt repurchases. The company agreed to an "omni blocker," equal treatment in future buyback offers and changes to roughly two dozen loan provisions. The proposed extension pushes a 2028 maturity to 2030 at 425 to 450 basis points over the benchmark and an issue price of 98 to 98.5.

Proofpoint's terms reveal a wider maturity and bargaining problem. Roughly $300 billion of US leveraged loans mature in 2028, with almost one-third tied to technology companies, many of them private-equity-backed software borrowers financed in 2021. Imprivata recently extended a $1.2 billion loan by paying 375 basis points over the benchmark, up from 300. The immediate concern is not only whether AI reduces future revenue. It is whether borrowers can refinance without moving collateral, favoring selected lenders or transferring value away from the existing capital structure.

European leveraged finance produced the same lender preference through scheduled principal repayment. Paysafe offered annual amortization equal to 5% of original principal to extend $814 million and EUR586 million of term loans by two years to 2030. The deal paid 500 basis points over the benchmark and allowed lenders to advance 95 while potentially receiving 100 at repayment. Investors also indicated that they would seek amortization if think-cell extends its EUR720 million loan, which currently pays 425 basis points over Euribor.

The return of meaningful amortization, rare in Europe since 2008, shifts risk from a single terminal refinancing toward earlier cash recovery. It also distinguishes profitable software borrowers able to repay debt from structures that depend on perpetual extension. CLO demand can still moderate lender power: about 30% of investors declined Carlyle-backed AutoForm's extension, yet broader demand allowed its EUR672 million term loan to tighten and move the maturity to 2032. Protection is becoming more expensive, but scarcity of loan supply still prevents a uniform tightening.

SoftBank's yen sale showed that diversification remains possible at a visible price. The company issued JPY90 billion, increasing the 3-year tranche to JPY80 billion while keeping the 5-year at JPY10 billion. Coupons of 3.270% and 3.886%, at spreads of 165 and 190 basis points over JGBs, were the highest paid by a domestic corporate borrower at those maturities this year. Investors preferred the shorter tranche in a rising-rate environment, and final demand for the 5-year portion covered it only about 1.2 times.

The sale helps finance SoftBank's more than $60 billion of commitments to OpenAI alongside a $40 billion bridge loan that has added 21 lenders. It also follows stalled talks for at least $6 billion of margin financing after an earlier $10 billion target was reduced. Access across yen, dollar, euro, retail subordinated and bank markets reduces dependence on any one channel. The high coupons and short-tenor preference show that funding breadth has not eliminated the market's concern about leverage, duration and the concentration of AI commitments.

Banks were also moving risk off balance sheet to preserve lending capacity. ING was preparing significant-risk-transfer transactions on about $10 billion of loans: roughly $6 billion of US and European project finance including data centers and €3.5 billion of Dutch SME exposure. The risk pieces represented about 7% and 6% of the reference portfolios, while global SRT issuance was projected to reach a record $45 billion in 2026 from $41 billion in 2025. Coupons above 10% attracted investors, but the mechanism transfers first-loss exposure rather than eliminating the underlying credit cycle. The private-credit-to-insurance channel carried a governance constraint of its own. After a reporting restatement, affiliated assets at Delaware Life were estimated by rating agencies at 40% to 42% of total assets rather than roughly 3% to 5%. Broader regulatory scrutiny of affiliated holdings could slow the pipeline through which asset managers place private loans onto insurer balance sheets, even without a change in borrower defaults. Credit liquidity was therefore functional but no longer passive. High-grade supply strained market functioning, CoreWeave paid more and strengthened documents, software lenders recovered collateral and repayment protections, and SoftBank broadened funding at the year's highest domestic coupons for comparable maturities. The common mechanism is not imminent default. It is the higher compensation, transferred loss exposure and tighter control required when large capital programs, refinancing walls and technological uncertainty compete for the same balance sheets.

## Global Duration, Central Banks, And Fiscal Transmission

Australia delivered the clearest counterexample to the US inflation steepening. Annual trimmed-mean CPI rose 3.6% in Q2, below the 3.7% consensus, and increased 0.8% quarter on quarter against a 0.9% forecast. Traders cut the probability of another RBA increase this year to about 50% from more than 90%, the Australian dollar fell as much as 0.5%, and the policy-sensitive 3-year yield dropped 11 basis points. The release reopened room to wait at the August 11 meeting after three increases earlier in 2026.

The composition kept the relief conditional. Tradables inflation was only 1.5% year on year, aided by lower imported-energy pressure and temporary fuel-tax relief, while non-tradables inflation reached 4.9%. Core inflation also remained above the RBA's 2% to 3% target band, and the renewed oil rise challenged the assumption that the external component would keep falling. Australia's curve repriced a softer domestic release, not the end of its tightening risk.

Euro-area wage evidence reduced the probability of a 2022-style second-round shock without closing the September policy question. The ECB's tracker projected negotiated pay growth of 2.6% in Q3 and Q4 and 2.7% in Q1 2027, far below the 5.2% peak in 2024. Officials described the increase as partly mechanical because old one-off payments were leaving the comparison. Stable wage pressure gives the ECB time to distinguish temporary energy inflation from persistence, although policymakers remain prepared to raise rates again if the outlook fails to improve.

Britain retained a less comfortable mix of high borrowing costs and resilient private credit demand. June mortgage approvals recovered to 58,200 from a more than two-year low and exceeded the 57,100 consensus, while unsecured borrowing increased by GBP1.8 billion. The average 5-year mortgage rate nevertheless reached 5.66% on July 29, up from 4.83% before the Iran war. Household and business borrowing has not collapsed, leaving the BOE to balance sluggish growth against energy pass-through rather than receiving a clear demand-side case for relief.

Japan's wage and institutional-buyer evidence both support a higher-volatility domestic duration regime. A labor ministry panel recommended a 4.9% rise in the nationwide minimum wage to JPY1,176 an hour, a JPY55 increase and the second-largest on record. The increase is smaller than last year's 6.3% but would broaden pay gains beyond large employers after major unions secured raises above 5% for a third year. That strengthens the BOJ's wage-price argument even as the bank assesses its June increase to a 1% policy rate.

GPIF's response shows how the buyer base is adapting. The fund appointed three active domestic bond managers for the first time in five years after losing 5.1% on Japanese bonds in the year to March, despite earning 16.5% overall. Its 25% domestic-bond allocation target gives it scale to support the market, but active mandates allow greater adjustment of maturity and credit exposure. Higher local yields can attract domestic savings while reducing the automatic foreign-duration demand that Treasuries once received from Japanese institutions.

Canada added a policy split inside an unchanged-rate decision. The Bank of Canada had held at 2.25% for a 6th meeting and projected growth to accelerate from 0.7% in 2026 to 1.8% in both 2027 and 2028. Some officials questioned whether the recovery was durable, while others saw medium-term inflation expectations drifting higher; excess supply, slower unit labor costs and easing rent inflation argued in the opposite direction. The current stance was still judged appropriate, but the minutes showed that the next adjustment depended on which side of the recovery-inflation tension persisted. The net global impulse is dispersion around a common energy shock. Australia received a genuine data-led rally, euro wages argued against automatic acceleration, and UK credit demand limited the case for rapid easing. Japan's wage breadth and institutional adaptation supported continued normalization. These channels do not mechanically force US yields higher, but they leave foreign policy rates and domestic bond returns sufficiently competitive to prevent the Treasury long end from relying on a uniform global duration bid.

## EM Sovereigns, Dollar Liquidity, And Debt-Management Risk

Emerging markets separated currency relief from hard-currency duration losses. A developing-market currency gauge rose 0.3% after the Fed held, while the US Dollar Index fell 0.59% to 100.78. EMB nevertheless lost 0.66%, and the 15-year-plus EM dollar sovereign index declined 0.60% as the rise in long Treasury yields overwhelmed the softer dollar. The common shock was therefore the discount rate at the long end, not a broad shortage of dollar liquidity.

Bolivia illustrated the limits of policy support when the market still questions implementation. Its bonds edged lower after the IMF announced agreement on a new $1.9 billion program. The reaction did not resemble a regional funding closure; EM currencies were firmer and the dollar weaker. It instead showed that headline access to official financing does not erase sovereign-specific execution and debt-sustainability concerns when investors lack a completed improvement in the balance-sheet path.

Brazil carried a different tension between easing inflation and resilient demand. Early-July consumer inflation slowed to 4.52% from 4.8% in mid-June, reinforcing expectations for a fourth consecutive 25-basis-point cut to 14% on August 5. A solid labor market and government fiscal and credit stimulus still threatened to keep demand firm relative to the 3% target. Lower US front-end yields offer some room, but higher long-dollar yields and rebounding oil keep the local easing path dependent on domestic disinflation rather than global relief alone.

Indian bank capital showed selective local-currency absorption. State Bank of India raised INR46.91 billion through perpetual Additional Tier 1 bonds after nearly two years away from the market. The 7.75% securities carry a 5-year call, are rated AA+ locally, and drew bids exceeding twice the INR30 billion base size. The capital supports a loan book that grew almost 17% to more than INR49 trillion. This is bank, not sovereign, risk, but it demonstrates that domestic savings can fund balance-sheet expansion even as dollar-duration assets weaken.

The Philippines showed how tax relief can weaken a planned fiscal consolidation before debt access closes. Proposed worker income-tax cuts could reduce annual revenue by as much as 60 billion pesos, or about $978 million, while the government was already planning 2.68 trillion pesos of 2026 borrowing. Debt stood at 65.2% of GDP in Q1, above the commonly cited 60% developing-economy threshold, and interest consumed a rising share of revenue as cheap pandemic debt refinanced at current yields. Reducing the deficit from 5.6% of GDP in 2025 toward 3.5% by 2030 therefore required replacement revenue or spending restraint alongside relief. India moved in the opposite direction by preparing legislation to formalize tax cuts for foreign investors in sovereign bonds, using fiscal policy to broaden external demand rather than household relief. The measure could improve buyer participation, but final enactment and actual flows—not the legislative plan alone—would establish its financing effect. EM conditions were consequently neither a broad risk-on move nor a common funding break. Currency markets welcomed the Fed hold, but hard-currency bonds remained exposed to the 30-year Treasury shock. Bolivia, Brazil and SBI then separated official-program credibility, domestic policy space and local capital absorption. The dollar's decline softened one external constraint; it did not neutralize long-duration repricing or country-specific balance-sheet tests.

## Cross asset

Cross assets reinforced the inflation-and-duration interpretation rather than a simple growth scare. Brent rose 7.37% and WTI 6.35% as geopolitical tensions resumed, reversing much of the immediate premise behind the prior Treasury rally. Gold gained 2.78% to $4,148.60 and the dollar fell 0.59%. Higher oil, higher gold and a weaker dollar alongside rising long yields are consistent with a larger inflation and credibility premium, not with a uniform demand for dollar cash.

Equities supplied an independent tightening signal. The S&P 500 fell 1.52%, the Nasdaq 100 lost 2.06%, and the semiconductor index dropped 5.33% for a fifth consecutive decline. The VIX rose 13.45% to 20.66. Semiconductor weakness reached 15.82% over 1 week and 20.87% over 1 month, linking concern about AI capital returns to the credit market's demands for wider discounts, stronger documents and earlier principal repayment. The broader equity decline after the Fed decision showed that lower front-end yields did not translate into easier financial conditions.

Credit and EM funds declined without the signature of indiscriminate liquidation. High-yield ETFs fell much less than duration-heavy LQD, emerging-market currencies rose, and the dollar weakened. The cross-asset check therefore supports two concentrated pressure points: energy and policy credibility in long sovereign yields, and AI spending and disruption in technology-linked risk. It does not support an economy-wide collapse in funding access.

## Forward Market Significance

The July 31 Employment Cost Index and subsequent inflation and labor releases determine whether the curve's policy-date split can persist. Wage or price evidence that remains firm while Brent holds near or above $90 would keep September active and require the 2-year yield to reverse its post-meeting decline; a softer labor-cost path combined with renewed oil de-escalation would allow the front end to extend its rally. The more consequential credibility threshold lies farther out: 10-year breakevens and 20- to 30-year real yields must stop rising for a delayed hike to look like patience rather than lost inflation control. The next quarterly refunding adds the supply side of the same test. Preserving the phrase that coupon sizes will remain steady for "at least the next several quarters" may contain an immediate announcement shock, whereas language that brings larger duration supply closer would reinforce the 2s30s steepening against the estimated $3.7 trillion four-year funding gap.

CoreWeave's Thursday order deadline and the potential $5.4 billion QTS financing tied to a Microsoft-leased data center measure whether AI credit has found a new clearing level. CoreWeave needs demand at up to 550 basis points over the benchmark, a 97 issue price and strengthened protections to show that concession can still offset concern about more than $34 billion of annual infrastructure spending. QTS would bring about $4.9 billion of secured bonds and a $500 million term loan after its recent loan fell to 97.75 from 99.5 and its April bond widened from roughly 138 to 239 basis points over Treasuries. Stable secondary prices and contained new-issue concessions would keep the strain concentrated in structure and price; another delay, wider discount or demand for additional creditor control would deepen the investment-grade and leveraged-loan absorption problem.

The Bank of England decision on July 30 and the Bank of Japan decision on July 31 define whether foreign duration becomes a larger competitor for US balance sheets. A BOE hold accompanied by confidence that energy pass-through will fade must lower gilt yields despite a 5.66% average 5-year mortgage rate and resilient borrowing; otherwise the UK curve retains its inflation and fiscal premium. The BOJ is expected to hold after June's increase to 1%, but guidance must reconcile a proposed 4.9% minimum-wage rise with the weak-yen import channel. A policy path that stabilizes the yen without another disorderly JGB selloff would reduce global term-premium pressure. Higher Japanese yields or renewed currency weakness would keep domestic returns attractive to Japanese institutions and leave the Treasury long end with less foreign-demand relief.

overall_summary.headline: Fed hold lowers short yields as inflation risk drives a historic curve steepening
overall_summary.session_narrative: Treasuries closed with the 2-year rallying and the 5- through 30-year sector selling off after the Fed held, because the decision removed an immediate hike but left the timing of restraint unresolved. Oil's rebound fed inflation compensation, and the Chair's reliance on market tightening transferred the burden toward long real yields and fiscal duration supply. Credit remained open at steeper discounts and stronger protections, while dollar weakness and overseas curve dispersion limited the case for a broad funding seizure.
overall_summary.summary: The 9-3 hold removed the immediate hike tail, yet limited guidance shifted restraint rather than erased it. Rebounding oil, higher breakevens and long real yields pushed duration costs higher, while heavy credit supply added an absorption strain. A softer dollar and divergent foreign curves argue against a generalized liquidity shock.
